chunks: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar narrated from Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“If you fear janabah, then say in your bed: O Allah, indeed I seek refuge in You from wet dreams, from evil dreams, and from Shaytan playing with me in wakefulness and sleep.”

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Shaytan, from whose interference the supplicant seeks protection
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah, the opening invocation of the supplication
key_terms.الِاحْتِلَامِ: a wet dream causing janabah during sleep
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةَ: the state of ritual impurity referred to here as something one fears occurring during sleep
key_terms.الْمَنَامِ: sleep, the other state in which protection is sought
key_terms.الْيَقَظَةِ: wakefulness, one of the two states in which protection is sought
key_terms.فِرَاشِكَ: your bed, indicating the time and place for reciting this supplication

ai.seo_question: What should a person say before sleep if they fear janabah or bad dreams?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a specific du'a to recite before sleep when one fears experiencing janabah through a wet dream or being disturbed by harmful dreams. It reflects seeking Allah's protection from both physical ritual impurity and satanic disturbance in both wakefulness and sleep.
